headline: Compete with confidence.
introduction: Practices are where coaches teach, players experiment, and teams prepare. Games are where players trust that preparation and play with confidence.
practices: Teams will generally practice one or two times per week ahead of tournament play.
practice_items: Flag pulling, coverage, and open-field movement
attendance: Families should communicate conflicts early—especially tournament availability—so coaches can plan practices, positions, and playing rotations. Consistent attendance is important for personal development and team cohesion; however, RFGF is understanding and supportive of multi-sport athletes and summer family time.
playing_time: Every rostered player will receive meaningful opportunities to compete. Playing time may not be equal in every game, and roles may vary based on preparation, attendance, the opponent, game situation, positional needs, and what supports player and team success.
